body:
Finding D scoping pass (pass_153) done -- you asked for investigate + scope only, not wire-it-in. Here's what it split into:

D1 (ConsolidatedMarketAnalysis/PatternRecognition): RESOLVED, confirmed safe. This part IS superseded by a richer live system (8-timeframe directional bias + advanced candlestick pattern analysis, both running every bar already). No action needed -- corrected my earlier "no replacement found" claim, that was wrong for this part.

D2 (PredictPatternFormation/ForecastRegimeChanges/UpdateNeuralNetworkSimulation): fully built and ALREADY WIRED into live consumers, but permanently gated off by one flag (predictiveSystem.predictionsValid) that's set false at init and never flipped true. Fails safely closed (neutral, not corrupting). One missing line would activate it. Well-scoped candidate for a future pass -- not wired now.

D3 -- the one that actually matters right now: CalculateIntelligentRisk is dead, and its absence leaves g_Risk.minRisk permanently stuck at 0.0 (never assigned anywhere else in the file). That value feeds directly into CalculateKellyCeiling's "no edge" branch -- the SAME Kelly ceiling you already have live from WARRANT#160 this week. Net effect: right now, whenever the system genuinely has no edge, it sizes the trade to exactly zero instead of the small conservative floor the code intends. This can only ever undershoot (never oversize -- the MathMin guarantee from R-8 still holds), so it's not a safety risk, but it's a real, previously-unverified gap in something I'd already marked "verified passing."

D4 (CalculateCorrelationRisk, IsBuffaloSetup, etc.): genuinely orphaned, self-admitted placeholders, low priority either way.

Everything above is disclosed in-source now (comments only, 0 errors/0 warnings, redeployed byte-identical everywhere) but NOT wired live -- I did not ship the D3 fix without asking, since it's a real behavior change to an already-live system even though it's narrow (a one/two-line struct-seeding fix). Want me to go ahead and ship the D3 fix (seed g_Risk.minRisk/maxRisk to sane values), or hold it too?
